diagnostic_evidence.quote:
As shown in \cite{pan2024block}, for general $\mathbf{v}\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times 1}$, $F_{\unitp,m}\vectocirc{\mathbf{v}}F_{\unitp,m}^{*}$ has 
	  an $X$-shape sparse matrix with sparse pattern shown as follows:

it has been proven in \cite{pan2024block} that any circulant quaternion matrix is fast block diagonalizable by means of fast Fourier transforms (FFTs), with each eigen-block being of size at most $2\times 2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims a diagonalization result for Strang's preconditioner and a contrast with 'general quaternion circulant matrices'. Strang's preconditioner c(T_n) is itself a quaternion circulant matrix, and the paper's own cited result (pan2024block, reproduced in the body) is that every quaternion circulant matrix is only block-diagonalized by the discrete quaternion Fourier transform, into 2x2 eigen-blocks — the paper's own Lemma-proof obtains 2x2 blocks for M(c(T_n)) and explicitly states that for general v 'applying Fourier transform to the first column ... would no longer obtain a vector with components in sigma(C(v))'. No diagonalizability statement is ever proved, and the cited block-diagonalization fact contradicts the claimed Strang-vs-general distinction.

failure_location.quote:
We show that Strang's circulant preconditioners can be diagionalized by 
discrete quaternion Fourier transform matrices 
whereas general quaternion circulant matrices cannot be diagonalized by them.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the abstract (and the corresponding intro sentence) to claim the block diagonalization that is actually established: Strang's preconditioner is fast block diagonalized by the DQFT into 2x2 eigen-blocks, like any quaternion circulant matrix.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract (and the echoing sentence in the introduction) misdescribes the paper's content; no formal result is invalidated, but the advertised contribution is false as stated.
issues.title: Abstract overclaims DQFT-diagonalizability of Strang's preconditioner
issues.why_classification: A local rewording to the statement the paper actually supports removes the false claim with no loss of mathematical content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: It is clear that $G[f](x)$ is Hermitian for each $x.$

issues.failure_explanation: The symbol is mis-assembled and the identity is false. (a) Hermiticity: since phi_2(f) is odd (Lemma gfuncstructurelm) but takes generally complex values, G12 = -phi_2(f)(x) and G21 = conj(phi_2(f)(x)) = -(-conj(phi_2(f)(x)))...; concretely G21 = conj(phi_2) equals -G12 only if phi_2(f)(x) is purely imaginary, which the structure lemma does not give; in general G12 = -G21 (up to sign conventions the off-diagonal entries are negatives, not conjugates), so G[f](x) is not Hermitian unless phi_2(f) == 0, and 'lambda_min(G[f](x)) = check f(x)' is ill-posed. (b) Counterexample to (i): take the absolutely summable data eta(0)=0, eta(1)=j (j an imaginary unit), so f(x) = j e^{ix} - j e^{-ix} satisfies Definition quatgfuncdef with t_0 = 0, t_1 = j; then phi_1(f) == 0 and phi_2(f)(x) = -2 sin(x) i. The generated matrix is T_2 = [[0,-j],[j,0]]. For y = (1,j)^T the left-hand side is y* T_2 y = 4 (T_2 y = (1, j)^T since (-j)*j = 1). The paper's integrand with phi_1(F)= e^{ix}, phi_2(F) = -i sin 2x, G12 = -phi_2(f) = 2i sin x, G21 = conj(-2i sin x) = 2i sin x, G22 = phi_1(f)(-x) = 0 gives u* G u = 0 + (2is)(iS)e^{-ix} + (-iS)(2is)e^{ix}·type pieces whose constant Fourier mode is 1/2, so the right-hand side is 1/2, not 4: the displayed integrals for 'term 2' and 'term 3' (extracted from mode sums s+l through the one-sided symbols) cannot reproduce the cross terms, which by the paper's own block identity (eq. tnfiledvalueeq1) pair entries t_{|s-l|} via Fourier differences. The proof's own assembly is also inconsistent: the intermediate 2x2 matrix in the display has entry +phi_2(f)(x) where the final G[f](x) has -phi_2(f)(x). Hence parts (i)-(iii), which rest on this symbol (including the ill-posed statement lambda_min(G[f](x)) = check f for a non-Hermitian symbol), fail.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must re-derive the correct quaternion symbol for y* T_n y (the assembled 2x2 symbol with entries phi_1(f)(±x) and the one-sided phi_2 pairings does not reproduce the cross terms), restate and re-prove (i)-(iii) for that symbol, and re-prove Corollary tnhpdcorol, Theorem quatszegothm and the circulant-spectrum characterization against the corrected symbol.
issues.overall_effect: The central quaternion spectral theorem (Rayleigh-quotient bounds, the functions check f / hat f, the strictness statement) is false; consequently the positive-definiteness criterion (Corollary tnhpdcorol), the quaternion Grenander-Szego theorem quatszegothm, the hypothesis 'check f positive' in Theorem strangcircprecedmatspectrumthm and the superlinear bound in Theorem strangcircmainthm, and the HPD guarantees claimed in Examples ar1 and ar2 are all unsupported.
issues.title: The symbol G[f](x) of Theorem 2.2 is mis-assembled; the quadratic-form identity is false
issues.why_classification: The central theorem is false as stated and the error is structural (the symbol's mode pairing is wrong, so no local fix restores the claimed identity); every spectral result downstream of check f / hat f collapses with it, and the source contains no contained repair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $c(T_n)$ is Hermitian and the eigenvalues of $c(T_n)$ are real.

Their eigenvalues
are given by 
$\phi_1(f_m) \left(\frac{2\pi s}{n}\right)$, 
$-\phi_2(f_m) \left(\frac{2\pi s}{n}\right)$, 
$\overline{\phi_2(f_m) \left(\frac{2\pi s}{n}\right)}$
and 
$\overline{\phi_1(f_m) \left(\frac{2\pi s}{n}\right)}$ 
($s=0,1,...,n-1$) respectively

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed identity sigma(c(T_n)) = union_{s<=floor(n/2)} sigma(G[f_m](2 pi s/n)) is false. (1) With the paper's own Definition of G (Theorem qhermitmatrayleightogfuncthm(i)), the (2,2)-entry is phi_1(f_m)(-theta_s), whereas the diagonalization in the proof delivers blocks with (2,2)-entry overline{phi_1(f_m)}(theta_s) = phi_1(f_m)(theta_s) (real-valued by Lemma gfuncstructurelm(i)); the two coincide only if phi_1(f_m) is even, which fails in general. (2) The proof also mis-computes the Strang symbols of the conjugated blocks: c(overline{phi_2(T_n)}) has the entrywise-conjugated symmetric kernel m_{-h} = -m_h, whose Strang symbol is a symmetrized (cosine-type) sum, not the point value overline{phi_2(f_m)}(theta_s) claimed in the proof. Concrete counterexample: eta(0)=0, eta(1)=j (absolutely summable), n=3, so phi_1(f) = 0 and phi_2(f)(theta) = -2 sin(theta) i; c(T_3) = circ(0, j, -j) is Hermitian, hence has real spectrum by the Lemma's own first claim, but the paper's formula produces G[f_1](2 pi/3) = [[0, 2i sin(2pi/3)],[2i sin(2 pi/3), 0]] with eigenvalues ±2i sin(2 pi/3) = ± i sqrt(3), which are not real. The stated equality is therefore false and the proof's symbol identification is invalid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the characterization with the blocks actually delivered by the simultaneous block diagonalization (i.e. the 2x2 blocks [phi_1(f_m)(theta_s), -StrangSymbol(phi_2 kernel)(theta_s); conj, phi_1(f_m)(theta_s)] with the symmetrized phi_2-kernel symbol), re-prove the mode-pairing reduction, and re-derive (ii)'s limits with the corrected eigenvalue functions; Theorems strangcircprecedmatspectrumthm and strangcircmainthm then need re-proof with the corrected bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's characterization of the spectrum of Strang's preconditioner (one of its two headline results) is false; part (ii) (the limits of lambda_min/lambda_max of c(T_n)) and the spectral analysis that feeds Theorems strangcircprecedmatspectrumthm and strangcircmainthm inherit the defect.
issues.title: Lemma strangcireiglimitlm(i): spectrum formula uses wrong symbol entries and is false
issues.why_classification: A correct characterization is obtainable by a contained re-derivation: the paper's own diagonalization argument delivers the true blocks, only the symbol identification and part (ii)'s limit formulas are wrong; the resulting characterization is a limited weakening of the stated one, and the downstream convergence results survive with corrected constants.
